title: Operation binding
description: A layered binding that selects which operating mode (at an exact revision) implements an operation contract for a given target. Bindings resolve by deterministic precedence (EXECUTION-MODES.md D2): authorized-invocation > backlog-item-override > initiative-override > system-default. The resolver (agentops.ResolveBinding) snapshots the winning layer plus the exact mode revision and fails CLOSED on every ambiguous or invalid state — it never silently falls back to a lower layer or a default. A binding names an operation contract, a mode id, and a pinned mode revision only; it can NEVER name a Go function, service, shell command, or file path.

operation.description: The operation contract id this binding implements.

operation_version.description: Optional exact operation-contract version this binding targets. Omitted binds the operation id across versions.

owner.description: The scope that owns this override. Required for every layer except system-default (a system-default binding owns no scope). A backlog-item-override owner is a backlog item ref; an initiative-override owner is an initiative name; an authorized-invocation owner is the invoking session/run id.

mode.description: The operating mode chosen to implement the operation for this scope.

mode_revision.description: The exact mode revision (content digest or version tag) pinned at bind time. A deleted/missing revision at resolve time is a typed error requiring operator action, not a silent re-resolution to latest.

disabled.description: When true this binding explicitly refuses the operation for its scope (a fail-closed veto), rather than being absent.

then.description: A system-default binding owns no scope.

else.description: Every override layer must name the scope it applies to.

BindingLayer.description: Precedence layer, highest to lowest: authorized-invocation (an explicit authorized caller pins the mode for one run) > backlog-item-override (the item pins its own mode) > initiative-override (the initiative pins the mode for its members) > system-default (the fleet default).
